notes: Launch-day Artificial Analysis read for Meta Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full (released 2026-10-12), retrieved 2026-10-13. AA lists one variant per new model, both max; there is no AA effort ladder for them (variant pages are HTTP 404). Values are parsed from the model object embedded in each model page (curl with a browser User-Agent), not read from a rendered chart. Same-snapshot peer rows were parsed the same way in the same session: Muse Spark 1.3 (max, xhigh), Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1, Haiku 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra at every effort AA lists (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Claude rows carry AA's 'Default Fallback' label in effort_verbatim. Peer Intelligence Index values agree with the 2026-10-07 AA file to 0.003 (Haiku 5.5 low 29.4495 then, 29.4524 now), and the non-Elo per-evaluation values agree to the stored precision. The two Elo-scored evaluations were re-rated when AA added the Muse models: AA-Briefcase moved by at most 4.3 Elo and GDPval-AA by up to 29.8 Elo for the same model and effort (GPT-6 Astra max GDPval-AA 1541.89 on 2026-10-07, 1571.66 now; GPT-6.1 Sol max 1575.09, now 1593.06; Opus 5.5 max 1866.24, now 1866.27). Use the rows in this file, not the 2026-10-07 file, for Elo comparisons with Muse Wonder. Per-evaluation rows exist for every stored model and effort (ten evaluations). CritPt and AA-LCR are stored under new metric ids aa-critpt and aa-lcr. Cost per task is AA's figure at list price; Haiku 5.5 costs exclude Anthropic's long-context tier (see the 2026-10-07 file). Gemini 4 Argon (high, 52.56, $1.99 per task) is on AA but is not a catalog model; it appears in claims only. Index scores are not comparable with other boards; keep the comparability groups. Recheck on or after 2026-10-20.

claims.statement: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 (page label; the article says 'v4.3'): Muse Wonder Full (max) 55.80 (displayed 56), Muse Wonder (max) 52.39 (52), Muse Spark 1.3 (max) 48.09 (48; xhigh 45.07). The AA article reports a gap of 6 weeks between Muse Spark 1.3 and the two new models.
claims.implication: Use these as publisher-run rows labelled max. AA does not state a reasoning effort other than max for either new model.

claims.statement: AA lists ONLY a max variant for each new model. The model pages /models/muse-wonder-low, -medium, -high, -xhigh and /models/muse-wonder-full-low, -medium, -high, -xhigh, -max, and /models/muse-wonder-max, all return HTTP 404 on 2026-10-13, and the leaderboard model list carries only the slugs muse-wonder and muse-wonder-full for the Wonder family (muse-spark-1-3 and muse-spark-1-3-xhigh for Spark 1.3). There is therefore no AA effort ladder for Muse Wonder or Muse Wonder Full and no low or medium row. Muse Wonder's own reasoning-effort levels are listed under the OpenRouter file.
claims.implication: The cheap-tier question (does Muse Wonder at low or medium clear the bar) cannot be answered from AA. Recheck on or after 2026-10-20 for new effort variants.

claims.statement: Muse Wonder (max) costs $4.52 per Index task at list price $4 in / $0.20 cached in / $20 out per M. AA splits it: input $3.43 (cache writes $1.92, cache hits $1.44, uncached $0.07) and output $1.08. Output tokens per task: 54,232 (reasoning 28,681, answer 25,551). The article gives 7.69M input tokens per task for Muse Wonder (max) and 6.44M for Muse Wonder Full (max). The article calls Muse Wonder's cost 'higher than most similarly intelligent models' and 2.8x Muse Spark 1.3 (max, $1.60).
claims.implication: Input volume, not output tokens, drives the cost of Muse Wonder. Compare with Opus 5.5 max $5.98, Sonnet 5.5 max $5.46, Fable 5.1 max $7.63, GPT-6 Astra max $3.26, GPT-6.1 Sol max $0.72 in the score rows.

claims.statement: Muse Wonder Full has no per-token price on AA, so AA shows no cost per task for it (the article: 'Muse Wonder Full is not priced per token, so no Cost per Task figure is available'). Output tokens per Index task: 53,754 (reasoning 29,163, answer 24,591). AA's page object for Muse Wonder Full has no provider speed or latency data (provider benchmark type 'median', 0 hosting providers).
claims.implication: No dollar comparison is possible for Muse Wonder Full from AA; its access is the Muse Code subscription only.

claims.statement: AA article, verbatim highlights: Muse Wonder Full (max) 'improves on Muse Spark 1.3 (max) across all ten Intelligence Index evaluations'; Terminal-Bench 4.0 +24 points (33% to 57%), GDPval-AA v2.1 +176 Elo (1681 to 1857), AA-Briefcase +148 Elo (1581 to 1729). Muse Wonder (max): Terminal-Bench 4.0 33% to 52%, AutomationBench-AA 58% to 68%. Muse Wonder Full is #1 on CritPt (33%) and GDP.pdf (33%, nearest competitors 31-32%), #2 on GDPval-AA v2.1 (1857; within the confidence intervals of Opus 5.5 max 1866 and Sonnet 5.5 max 1838), #3 on AA-Briefcase (1729), AutomationBench-AA (71%) and SciCode (63%). Knowledge is a weakness: AA-Omniscience 30 (Full) and 25 (Wonder), against Opus 5.5 46, GPT-6 Astra 43, Gemini 4 Argon 42, Sonnet 5.5 32; hallucination rate 23% (Full; 33% for Spark 1.3) and 27% (Wonder), which AA calls the second-lowest among models scoring 45 or more on the index, behind Gemini 4 Argon (high, 15%).
claims.implication: Rank claims are AA statements about its own board on 2026-10-12. Per-evaluation values are in the score rows and agree with the article to its displayed precision.

claims.statement: Pricing, context and modalities per the AA article and model pages: Muse Wonder $4 input / $0.20 cached input / $20 output per 1M tokens (page object: price1m 4 / 20, cache hit 0.2, blended 7:2:1 $2.94 per 1M); context 1,048,576 tokens for Muse Wonder and 1,000,000 for Muse Wonder Full (the article says 1M for both); input modalities text, image, video, audio (AA's embedded flags: speech true, video true for both); output text only. Availability per AA: Muse Wonder on Meta's first-party API and Muse Code; Muse Wonder Full for Muse Code users only. AA's provider list for Muse Wonder has one provider (Meta first-party).
claims.implication: Matches the first-party price in the Meta lane. The context difference (1,048,576 vs 1,000,000) is an AA data field, not a Meta statement.

claims.statement: AA speed for Muse Wonder (max), first-party Meta endpoint: median output speed 104.1 tokens/s and median time to first chunk 19.7 s (long prompt type; AA's median end-to-end for the prompt types is on the page). Muse Spark 1.3 (max) for comparison: 127.3 tokens/s and 41.7 s. AA time per Index task: Muse Wonder (max) 502 s, Muse Spark 1.3 (max) 467 s.
claims.implication: AA and OpenRouter measure speed differently (OpenRouter: 67 tokens/s P50, 2.68 s latency; see the OpenRouter file). Do not merge.

claims.statement: Same-snapshot position of Muse Wonder Full (max) 55.8 against peer rows read the same day: Opus 5.5 max 57.6 / xhigh 56.0 / high 53.6 / medium 51.2 / low 42.3; Sonnet 5.5 max 56.0 / xhigh 51.9 / high 46.8; Fable 5.1 max 53.4 / xhigh 53.2 / high 51.2; GPT-6 Astra max 52.7; GPT-6.1 Sol max 51.8 / xhigh 51.0 / high 50.2; Haiku 5.5 max 43.4. Muse Wonder (max) 52.4 sits level with GPT-6 Astra max and Gemini 4 Argon (high, 52.6; not a catalog model). On cost per task Muse Wonder (max) $4.52 against Opus 5.5 high $1.82 (53.6) and medium $1.34 (51.2): at the same index level Opus 5.5 at high costs about 40% of Muse Wonder (max).
claims.implication: On AA at max, Muse Wonder Full (55.8) is third behind Opus 5.5 (57.6) and Sonnet 5.5 (56.0), 0.2 points under Sonnet 5.5; Muse Wonder (52.4) costs about 2.5x Opus 5.5 high ($1.82 per task) for a lower index score (53.6). This is evidence, not a routing change.

claims.statement: AA states nothing about a pre-release deployment, API fallback or effort mapping for the Muse Wonder runs. The labels carry only 'max'. AA did not flag the runs as provisional on the article or the model pages (read 2026-10-13). AA says Muse Wonder Full is available only to Muse Code users; the AA performance record for it is a 'median' type with no hosting provider.
claims.implication: Treat the rows as launch-day reads (retrieved 2026-10-13, one day after release). Recheck on or after 2026-10-20.
